## Q1
Match List-I (OS and distributed-systems terms) with List-II.

| List-I | List-II |
|---|---|
| A. System Call | I. A process requests a function that is located in a different computer system. |
| B. Preemption | II. A request that a program makes to the operating system. |
| C. Real time application | III. The forced deallocation of the CPU from a process. |
| D. Remote procedure call | IV. A program that responds to activities in an external system within a maximum time determined by that external system. |

## Q1 - Options
(A) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
(B) A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I
(C) A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I
(D) A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV

## Q1 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** OS: Linux, Windows, Security, Virtualization & Distributed
**Source:** UGC NET Jan 2026 (2 Jan, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q76

A system call is a request that a program makes to the operating system, so A pairs with II.<br>
Preemption is the forced deallocation of the CPU from a running process, so B pairs with III.<br>
A real-time application must respond to activities in an external system within a maximum time set by that external system, so C pairs with IV.<br>
A remote procedure call lets a process invoke a function located on a different computer system, so D pairs with I.

A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I is therefore the correct match.

## Q2
Which of the following is correct about Real time operating system?

A. It permits creation of multiple processes within an application.<br>
B. It does not permit priorities to be assigned to processes.<br>
C. It permits a programmer to define interrupts and interrupt processing routines.<br>
D. It does not use priority-driven or deadline-oriented scheduling.<br>
E. It provides fault tolerance and graceful degradation capabilities.

## Q2 - Options
(A) A, B & D Only
(B) B, C & D Only
(C) A, C & E Only
(D) B, D & E Only

## Q2 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** OS: Linux, Windows, Security, Virtualization & Distributed
**Source:** UGC NET Jan 2026 (2 Jan, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q79

A real-time operating system (RTOS) is built to guarantee timely, predictable responses to events, and checking each statement against that goal resolves the set.

- **A. It permits creation of multiple processes within an application.** — correct, an RTOS supports multitasking so an application can split its work across several cooperating processes or tasks.
- **B. It does not permit priorities to be assigned to processes.** — wrong, priority assignment is central to an RTOS since tasks with tighter deadlines must be able to preempt less urgent ones.
- **C. It permits a programmer to define interrupts and interrupt processing routines.** — correct, RTOS kernels expose interrupt service routine hooks so time-critical events can be handled directly.
- **D. It does not use priority-driven or deadline-oriented scheduling.** — wrong, priority-driven and deadline-oriented scheduling (for example rate-monotonic or earliest-deadline-first) are the defining scheduling techniques of an RTOS.
- **E. It provides fault tolerance and graceful degradation capabilities.** — correct, RTOS designs for critical systems build in fault tolerance so the system degrades gracefully instead of failing outright.

Only A, C and E hold, matching A, C & E Only.

## Q3
What does a superblock object represent in the virtual file system of a Linux OS?

## Q3 - Options
(A) an open file
(B) an entire file system
(C) individual directory entry
(D) an individual file

## Q3 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** OS: Linux, Windows, Security, Virtualization & Distributed
**Source:** UGC NET Jan 2026 (2 Jan, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q88

The Linux Virtual File System (VFS) uses four principal object types, and the superblock is the one that represents a whole mounted file system, holding metadata such as its type, size, and status.

An open file is represented by a file object, an individual file's metadata is held in an inode object, and a directory entry is represented by a dentry object, each of which is distinct from the superblock.

Because the superblock stores information describing an entire mounted file system, an entire file system is the correct answer.

## Q4
Arrange Linux interrupt-protection levels from increasing priority: user-mode programs, preemptible kernel system-service routines, bottom-half interrupt handlers, and top-half interrupt handlers.

## Q4 - Options
(A) B → A → C → D
(B) C → B → A → D
(C) C → A → B → D
(D) A → D → B → C

## Q4 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** OS: Linux, Windows, Security, Virtualization & Distributed
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2025 (26 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q45

User-mode work is the most preemptible and therefore lowest priority. Preemptible kernel service routines rank above it, bottom halves above ordinary kernel work, and top-half interrupt handlers are highest because they run immediately in interrupt context.

## Q5
Which of the following statements are TRUE about Privileged Instructions ?<br>
A. It can only be executed by the Operating<br>
System kernel and not by user applications.<br>
B. It is designed to perform operations that can directly affect the hardware or system state such as I/O operations or changing memory management setting.<br>
C. User applications can execute privileged instructions if they have to correct permissions, set by the Operating System.<br>
D. It usually executed in user mode to ensure the safety and security of the system.

## Q5 - Options
(A) (A) and (B) Only
(B) (A), (B) and (C) Only
(C) (B) and (C) Only
(D) (B), (C) and (D) Only

## Q5 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** OS: Linux, Windows, Security, Virtualization & Distributed
**Source:** UGC NET Aug 2024 (23 Aug, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q16

(A) is true — privileged instructions execute only in kernel (supervisor) mode. (B) is true — they cover exactly the operations touching hardware or system state, such as I/O and memory-management setup. (C) is false: no permission setting lets a user-mode application execute one directly; it must trap into the kernel. (D) is false: they run in kernel mode, not user mode. Only (A) and (B) — option A.

## Q8
Assertion (A): I/O protection is ensured by a hardware trap.<br>
Reason (R): I/O interrupt is caused by conditions like I/O completion and device malfunction occurring within the I/O devices.

## Q8 - Options
(A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
(B) Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
(C) A is true but R is false
(D) A is false but R is true

## Q8 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** OS: Linux, Windows, Security, Virtualization & Distributed
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q6

I/O protection and I/O interrupts are related but distinct hardware mechanisms in operating systems.

Assertion A is true because I/O instructions are privileged, so any attempt by a user program to execute one directly causes a hardware trap into the operating system, which then validates and performs the operation on the program's behalf.

Reason R is also true as a general statement, because I/O interrupts are indeed signals raised by a device to report events such as completion of a transfer or a malfunction.

R does not explain A because the trap mechanism that enforces I/O protection is triggered by a user program's attempt to run a privileged instruction, not by the device-generated completion or malfunction interrupts that R describes. These are two separate mechanisms serving different purposes, so R is true but not the reason A holds.

## Q9
Model of protection can be viewed as

## Q9 - Options
(A) Owner matrix
(B) Domain matrix
(C) Access Matrix
(D) Global matrix

## Q9 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** OS: Linux, Windows, Security, Virtualization & Distributed
**Source:** UGC NET Mar 2023 (15 Mar, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q17

The classical protection model represents the state of a system as an access matrix, with rows for protection domains and columns for objects, where each entry lists the operations a domain may perform on that object.

This access matrix model is the standard abstraction used to describe and reason about access rights across domains and resources in an operating system.

"Owner matrix", "domain matrix", and "global matrix" are not the standard terminology for this abstraction, since a domain is only one axis of the matrix rather than the model's name itself.

## Q10
In Linux Operating System, when \_\_\_\_\_\_ is invoked, it is passed a set of flags that determine how much sharing is to take place between the parent and child tasks.

## Q10 - Options
(A) fork()
(B) clone()
(C) pthread()
(D) thread()

## Q10 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** OS: Linux, Windows, Security, Virtualization & Distributed
**Source:** UGC NET Mar 2023 (11 Mar, Shift 2) · Paper 2 · Q17

Linux implements process and thread creation through a single system call, `clone()`, which takes explicit flag arguments such as CLONE_VM and CLONE_FS to control exactly which resources (address space, file descriptors, and signal handlers) the parent and child share.

`fork()` is implemented on top of `clone()` with a fixed set of flags, so it does not itself expose configurable sharing.

## Q11
The main function of the microkernel is to provide a communication facility between the \_\_\_\_\_\_ program and the various \_\_\_\_\_\_ that are also running in user space.

## Q11 - Options
(A) Virtual, Processes
(B) System, Processes
(C) Client, Services
(D) Virtual, Services

## Q11 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** OS: Linux, Windows, Security, Virtualization & Distributed
**Source:** UGC NET Mar 2023 (11 Mar, Shift 2) · Paper 2 · Q18

In microkernel design, the kernel is stripped down to minimal functionality, and traditional OS functions (file systems, device drivers, networking) run as separate user-space services.

The microkernel's main job is to relay messages between a client program and those user-space services, so it can be swapped or restarted independently of the core kernel.

## Q12
Select the correct order of events after power is initialized on a system.

A. Bootstrap loader is loaded from the disk<br>
B. Kernel is loaded onto the memory<br>
C. Firmware ROM loads boot block

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

## Q12 - Options
(A) B, C, A
(B) C, A, B
(C) A, B, C
(D) A, C, B

## Q12 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** OS: Linux, Windows, Security, Virtualization & Distributed
**Source:** UGC NET Mar 2023 (11 Mar, Shift 2) · Paper 2 · Q80

Booting proceeds from the most permanent, hardwired code toward the fully loaded operating system.

Firmware in ROM runs first and loads the boot block, which is C. That boot block then loads the bootstrap loader from disk, which is A. The bootstrap loader finally loads the kernel into memory, which is B.

The order is C, A, B.

## Q15
Which of the following CPU scheduling algorithms is/are supported by LINUX operating system?

## Q15 - Options
(A) Non-preemptive priority scheduling
(B) Preemptive priority scheduling and time sharing CPU scheduling
(C) Time sharing scheduling only
(D) Priority scheduling only

## Q15 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** OS: Linux, Windows, Security, Virtualization & Distributed
**Source:** UGC NET Dec 2019 (4 Dec, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q30

The Linux operating system kernel implements both preemptive priority scheduling and time-sharing scheduling. Real-time tasks are scheduled using preemptive priority policies (SCHED_FIFO and SCHED_RR), while normal user processes are managed via the Completely Fair Scheduler (CFS) using time-sharing proportional resource allocation.

## Q16
Which of the following methods are used to pass any number of parameters to the operating system through system calls?

## Q16 - Options
(A) Registers
(B) Block or table in main memory
(C) Stack
(D) Block in main memory and stack

## Q16 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** OS: Linux, Windows, Security, Virtualization & Distributed
**Source:** UGC NET Dec 2019 (4 Dec, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q51

Operating systems employ three common techniques to pass parameters during system calls:

1. Registers — fastest approach, but limited by the fixed count of hardware processor registers, making it incapable of passing arbitrary numbers of parameters.
2. Block or table in main memory — parameters are stored in a designated memory block, and a single pointer to the block is passed in a register. This permits passing any number of parameters.
3. Stack — parameters are pushed onto the program stack by the calling process and popped off by the operating system kernel, which also accommodates arbitrary numbers of parameters.

Therefore, both block in memory and stack methods accommodate any number of parameters.

## Q18
Which of the following UNIX/Linux pipes will count the number of lines in all the files having .c and .h as their extension in the current working directory?

## Q18 - Options
(A) cat \*.ch \| wc -l
(B) cat \*.[c-h] \| wc -l
(C) cat \*.[ch] \| ls -l
(D) cat \*.[ch] \| wc -l

## Q18 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** OS: Linux, Windows, Security, Virtualization & Distributed
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q76

Evaluating Unix shell wildcards and pipe operators:

- The character class glob pattern `*.[ch]` matches any file ending with either `.c` or `.h` in the current working directory.
- The `cat` command concatenates and streams the file contents to standard output.
- The pipe operator `|` redirects that output into `wc -l`, which counts the total number of lines.

`cat *.ch` looks for extension `.ch`, `*.[c-h]` matches any character from c through h, and piping into `ls -l` ignores incoming stdin stream data.

## Q19
In Linux operating system environment \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ command is used to print a file.

## Q19 - Options
(A) lpr
(B) ptr
(C) pr
(D) print

## Q19 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** OS: Linux, Windows, Security, Virtualization & Distributed
**Source:** UGC NET Dec 2018 (20 Dec, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q14

In Unix and Linux environments, the standard command used to spool and print a file is lpr (line printer remote).

- lpr submits print jobs to the CUPS or LPD print spooler daemon.
- Option B (ptr) is not a standard Unix command.
- Option C (pr) is used to paginate and format text files for printing, not to send them to the printer queue.
- Option D (print) is an alias or shell builtin in certain environments, not the standard Unix printing utility.

## Q20
Which of the following statement/s is/are true ?

(i) Windows XP supports both peer-peer and client-server networks.<br>
(ii) Windows XP implements Transport protocols as drivers that can be loaded and unloaded from the system dynamically.

Choose the correct answer from the code given below :<br>
Code :

## Q20 - Options
(A) Both (i) and (ii)
(B) (ii) only

## Q20 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** OS: Linux, Windows, Security, Virtualization & Distributed
**Source:** UGC NET Dec 2018 (20 Dec, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q74

Both statements describe standard networking capabilities and kernel architecture in Windows XP.

- Statement (i) is true because Windows XP supports workgroup peer-to-peer networking as well as joining Active Directory domain controllers in client-server environments.
- Statement (ii) is true because transport protocols (such as TCP/IP) in Windows NT/XP are implemented as NDIS/TDI device drivers that the kernel loads and unloads dynamically without requiring a system reboot.
- Therefore, both statements (i) and (ii) are true (Option A).
